Here's what happens. When an episode ends with a cliffhanger, your brain feels that the story isn't finished. And the brain hates unfinished stories. It wants to know what happens next, so you keep watching. Then autoplay makes it even easier. You don't need to decide to continue. You only need to do nothing. And doing nothing is the easiest thing in the world at eleven o'clock at night. So my advice is simple. Turn off autoplay, and decide how many episodes you will watch before you start, not after. It sounds small, but it really works.

My friends think I'm crazy. I've watched the same sitcom about six times. I know every joke. But that's exactly why I love it. After a hard day at work, I don't want to think. I don't want a plot twist or a cliffhanger. I just want to laugh with characters I know. It helps me relax. New series are different. They're great, but they're too addictive. If I start one on a Tuesday, I stay up until two in the morning. So during the week, I avoid starting new series. I keep those for the weekend, and on weeknights, I rewatch my old friends.

When I was a student, I watched a lot of American series, always with subtitles in my own language. I enjoyed the stories, but my English didn't improve much. One day, a teacher told me to try English subtitles. At first it was hard. I understood very little, and I wanted to give up. But I decided to keep going, one episode a day. I chose a sitcom that I already knew, so the story was easy to follow. After a few months, something changed. I stopped needing the subtitles for most of the dialogue. Today I teach English, and I still tell my students the same thing: keep watching, but change the subtitles.
